what_happened: A bespoke one-off Python relative-link resolver plus the existing lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh baseline run surfaced a systemic docs-README.md/README.md naming mismatch (13 broken breadcrumb links across 7 files) and a second duplication instance (Three-Layer Architecture explanation, not named in the dispatch) quickly, without needing to read every file at full depth.

Planning re-derivation found three defect sites the research report's enumeration missed: orchestrate-state-machine.md:239 presents /implement {N} as a runnable resume command inside 420's cycle-budget paragraph; orchestrate-state-machine.md:948-955 and :1393-1397 carry record-versioning prose ('used to', 'is retired', 'unchanged from before this design existed'); copy-claude-directory.md has 3 (not 2) ../commands/README.md occurrences. Also found that the record-versioning forbidden vocabulary occurs ~56 times corpus-wide, ~53 of them inside the three boundary-owned architecture files, which forces an explicit scope narrowing in the plan.

The research report's per-site classification (dead-surface vs phase-name vs path-literal vs boundary) held up under spot-check on every site verified, including the subtle docs-README.md case where ../README.md correctly resolves to core/README.md and must NOT be swept by the 13-occurrence breadcrumb fix. That saved a full reclassification pass at planning time.
